info.title: Eyes
info.description: Eyes pays a nearby human a few dollars to check something in a public place right now (is it open, how long is the line, is it in stock, how crowded is it) and returns a verified answer with a live photo. Paths are relative to this server's origin. Start with /llms.txt, and check GET /status for which parts of this server are live: a simulated deploy sends no texts and has no workers, and with simulated place lookup only {lat, lng} coordinates and the demo places "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco", "Ferry Building, San Francisco", "Trader Joe's, 401 Bay St, San Francisco" resolve. The same tools are available over MCP at POST /mcp.

tags.name: agent
tags.description: Called by AI agents with a bearer API key (signup is public).

post.description: MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint (JSON-RPC 2.0). Connect an MCP client here with the header Authorization: Bearer <api_key>; do not hand-craft requests. Model tools: quote_task, ask_eyes, report_classifier, get_classifier_report, await_answer, get_task, list_tasks, cancel_task, accept_answer, dispute_answer, get_balance, get_spend_policy, show_task. Additional app-only action: confirm_ask. Interactive ask_eyes prepares a read-only confirmation draft; REST and non-UI ask_eyes dispatch directly (schemas in /llms-full.txt).

schema.description: An MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 response, as JSON or text/event-stream.

post.description: Public, no API key needed. Creates an agent and returns api_key (shown only once, store it), top_up_url (a Stripe Checkout link for your human to fund the balance, when payments are live) and email_address (a private address for asking Eyes by email; null when email is not configured; anyone who knows it can spend your balance). Test mode grants 20 USD. Pass owner_email, your human's email address: when email is live (see GET /status), Eyes emails them a private control link to set your spend limits and add funds, and you never see that link. Then send Authorization: Bearer <api_key> on every other call.

email_address.description: Private address for asking Eyes by email. Anyone who knows it can spend your balance, so keep it secret.

post.description: Free and read-only. Check whether Eyes can answer at a place before you spend anything: workers_nearby, est_minutes_to_answer, suggested_bounty_usd, allowed with reason_if_not, and resolved_location (where Eyes thinks you mean). suggested_bounty_usd already fits this API key's max_bounty_usd, the daily cap left and your balance. allowed is false only when you cannot post this task right now (safety rules refuse the place or task_type, the task_type is not allowed for this key, or even the minimum bounty plus fee does not fit your limits or balance); reason_if_not says what to do. quote_task never sees your question, so ask_eyes checks the question itself and can still refuse it with unsafe_task. Next: if allowed is true and workers_nearby > 0, call ask_eyes with the same location and task_type. Same as the MCP tool quote_task.

anyOf.description: A public place as "place name, city" or its street address, e.g. "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco". Never a home address.

location.description: The public place to check: a string "place name, city" or its numbers {"lat": 37.7825, "lng": -122.4078}. Never the user's own location or a home address.

suggested_bounty_usd.description: A bounty ask_eyes accepts for this API key right now: the default, lowered to fit max_bounty_usd, the daily cap left after the fee, and your balance after the fee. Pass it as bounty_usd.

allowed.description: False when this API key cannot post this task right now: Eyes' safety rules refuse this task_type at this place, the task_type is not in allowed_task_types, or even the 1 USD minimum bounty plus fee does not fit max_bounty_usd, the daily cap left or the balance. It does not check your question: ask_eyes checks the question itself and can still refuse it with unsafe_task.

reason_if_not.description: Why allowed is false and what to do: change the place or task_type, top up at top_up_url, wait for the daily cap to reset at midnight UTC, or ask your user to raise a limit. Null when allowed is true.

post.description: For REST and non-UI MCP dispatch, pay a nearby human to look at a public place and answer your question, usually with a live photo. bounty_usd (default 3) plus a 0.50 USD fee is escrowed on dispatch, paid to the worker only after a verified answer, and refunded in full if nobody answers before deadline_minutes or you cancel before a worker claims it. idempotency_key is required: any unique string for each task you intend to create. Reuse it when you retry that task: the same key and parameters return the original task instead of charging again. Only public, commercial or civic places. resolved_location gives the stored task's label, latitude and longitude, including on retries. A place name can resolve to another city or country; Eyes does not reject a result for that mismatch. Check resolved_location before relying on the answer. Out-of-range coordinates are refused, including coordinate strings. NUL characters and lone Unicode surrogates are invalid input; remove them from the named field instead of retrying unchanged. REST returns 400 invalid_input with issues; MCP returns an input validation error with the field path. After dispatch, call await_answer with the returned task_id immediately. Interactive MCP instead prepares the read-only draft documented below; payment requires a later card confirmation. Same as non-UI MCP tool ask_eyes.

question.description: What the human should check, in plain words, e.g. "How many people are in line right now?"

anyOf.description: A public place as "place name, city" or its street address, e.g. "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco". Never a home address.

location.description: The public place to check: a string "place name, city" or its numbers {"lat": 37.7825, "lng": -122.4078}. Never the user's own location or a home address.

task_type.description: is_open: open or closed now; line_length: how long the line is; in_stock: whether an item is on the shelf; photo_of_place: a current photo; price_check: a posted price; crowd_level: how busy it is; other_public: any other check of a public place.

bounty_usd.description: Paid to the human who answers. A $0.50 fee is added. Both are escrowed now and refunded if nobody answers.

deadline_minutes.description: Minutes until the task expires and the escrow is refunded.

require_photo.description: Require a live photo. Keep true unless a text answer is enough; photos are what make an answer verifiable.

idempotency_key.description: Required. Any unique string for each task you intend to create, for example a UUID. Reuse it when you retry that task: the same key and parameters return the original task and never charge twice. Use a new key for a new question.

classifier_report_id.description: Approved classifier feedback ticket for this exact request and API agent. Never grants permission for a changed request.

example.question: How many people are waiting in line right now?
example.location: Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco

status.description: New tasks are dispatched. A retry returns the stored task status, without another charge or policy check.

get.description: Instant, read-only list of the tasks this API key created, newest first: task_id, status, question, place_label, bounty_usd, created_at, deadline_at and answered. Call it when you lost a task_id (context reset, crash) and before asking a question again, so you resume an open task instead of paying twice. status filters to one status; limit is 1 to 50 (default 20). Pass next_cursor as before for older tasks with the same status filter; null means no more tasks. Cursors refer to a task owned by this API key; an unknown cursor returns an empty page. Next: await_answer any task still dispatched, claimed or submitted; get_task any task where answered is true. Same as the MCP tool list_tasks.

schema.description: Only return tasks in this status, e.g. "dispatched" for tasks no worker has claimed yet. Omit for every status.
How many tasks to return, newest first. 1 to 50.
Cursor from next_cursor for the next page. Keep the same status filter. Omit for the newest tasks.

answered.description: True when status is verified, paid or needs_review; get_task returns the answer.

next_cursor.description: Pass as before for older tasks; null means no more tasks.

post.description: Create an internal Support ticket with the original refused Ask and client-reported unsafe_task context. Reuse one report idempotency_key per card; ask_idempotency_key is the original Ask key. No dispatch, messages or charge. A human may approve this exact request for the same agent for 24 hours. Next: explicitly check get_classifier_report. Same as the MCP tool report_classifier.

get.description: Read your ticket status. On approved, explicitly retry the unchanged original Ask with classifier_report_id equal to ticket_id and the original Ask idempotency_key. Rejected or expired does not permit retry. Consumed returns the existing task_id. Normal deterministic safety rules, spending limits and balance always apply. Same as the MCP tool get_classifier_report.

post.description: Read-only bounded wait for an existing dispatched task_id, not a draft intent key. It checks recorded state about once a second for up to timeout_seconds (default 50, max 55); the request can be cancelled earlier. It does not dispatch, pay, refund or keep watching after the response. answered is true for verified, paid or needs_review, but answer and photo_url can be null. verified does not prove payout; paid records payout; needs_review requires human settlement. Re-call the same task_id while dispatched, claimed or submitted; stop on expired, refunded or disputed. get_task and show_task can also read the current answer. Same as the MCP tool await_answer.

schema.description: Existing task_id from confirmed dispatch or a task lookup. Not a draft idempotency_key.

timeout_seconds.description: How long this call waits for an answer, at most 55 seconds. Call again while answered is false and the status is dispatched, claimed or submitted; stop on expired, refunded or disputed.

gps_ok.description: The worker was within about 150 m of the place.

fresh_ok.description: The photo was taken live, before the deadline.

vision_ok.description: The photo check completed without confirmed graphic gore or explicit sexual content. Content uncertainty alone passes; provider failures need review. It does not mean the answer is correct.

vision_reason.description: Why the photo is or is not safe to share.

accepted_at.description: When your agent accepted this answer. Feedback only; not photo verification or payment.

get.description: Instant, read-only status and details of one task, including the answer once there is one. To wait for an answer call await_answer instead of polling get_task. Same as the MCP tool get_task.

deadline_minutes.description: Minutes until the task expires and the escrow is refunded.

status.description: open: a person is reviewing your dispute. upheld: the answer was fake; bounty and fee were refunded to your balance. rejected: the answer stands and the worker keeps the pay.

refunded_usd.description: What was refunded to your balance when the dispute was upheld.

dispute.description: Your dispute_answer on this task and its outcome; null if you never disputed it.

post.description: Cancel a task that no worker has claimed yet (status dispatched) and refund the full escrow, bounty plus fee. After a worker claims it this fails with task_not_cancellable; keep calling await_answer instead. Same as the MCP tool cancel_task.

Record your user's positive feedback on an owned answered task with status verified or paid. Returns status accepted and the first accepted_at timestamp. Repeated calls are idempotent; get_task and await_answer retain accepted_at. This is not machine verification, never changes payment, and does not remove the right to dispute. Next: accept only after your user says the answer looks good. Same as the MCP tool accept_answer.

status.description: Your agent's positive feedback, not machine verification.

post.description: Flag an answered task (status verified, paid or needs_review) as wrong. The worker payout is held and the task goes to human review. Give a specific reason. To get a fresh answer now, call ask_eyes again with a new idempotency_key. Same as the MCP tool dispute_answer.

reason.description: What is wrong with the answer, e.g. "photo shows a different store".

example.reason: The photo shows a different cafe, not Blue Bottle.

deadline_minutes.description: Minutes until the task expires and the escrow is refunded.

require_photo.description: Require a live photo. Keep true unless a text answer is enough; photos are what make an answer verifiable.

get.description: Your prepaid balance and the amount escrowed in open tasks, in USD, plus top_up_url: a link your human opens to add funds with Stripe Checkout. If balance_usd is below bounty_usd + 0.50, give your human top_up_url, and after they pay call get_balance again before asking. Same as the MCP tool get_balance.

The limits your human set on this API key: max_bounty_usd per task, daily_cap_usd, spent_today_usd and remaining_today_usd (UTC day), and allowed_task_types. Stay within them when you call ask_eyes; only your human can change them. Same as the MCP tool get_spend_policy.

max_bounty_usd.description: Most one task may pay a worker; null means no limit.

daily_cap_usd.description: Spend cap for the cap_period; null means no limit.

spent_today_usd.description: Spent so far in the current cap_period.

remaining_today_usd.description: Left under the cap in the current cap_period; null means no limit.

Error.description: Error. Status by code: unauthorized 401, invalid_input 400, not_found 404, method_not_allowed 405, payload_too_large 413, service_unavailable 503, insufficient_balance 402, bounty_exceeds_max 403, daily_cap_exceeded 403, task_type_not_allowed 403, unsafe_task 422, location_not_found 422, no_workers_nearby 409, task_not_found 404, task_not_cancellable 409, task_not_disputable 409, task_not_acceptable 409, email_taken 409, idempotency_conflict 409, offer_invalid 404, task_already_claimed 409, rate_limited 429, owner_link_invalid 404, not_implemented 501, internal_error 500.
